samples.summary: `anchoredFramePatch` — the panel-side fix for #1039 and its new non-finite fallback — has no test anywhere
samples.evidence: grep for `anchoredFramePatch` finds only the definition (frame-patch.ts:27), two call sites in format-panel/index.tsx (128, 237) and docs; no test file matches `**/frame-patch*` (only the source file). The frontend already has a natural home for it (`packages/frontend/tests/app/slides/format-panel/{units,pick-sections}.test.ts`) and a running vitest lane, so the gap is not for lack of infra. Consequently nothing covers: (a) a size-only pass-through when w/h are undefined, (b) the anchored x/y on a rotated frame (the actual user-visible #1039 panel bug), (c) the new `!Number.isFinite(next.x||next.y)` degrade-to-size-only branch added by this delta, whose claimed behaviour is even documented in docs/design/slides/slides-format-options-panel.md:260. If that guard were inverted or the helper regressed, a rotated element resized from the panel would jump or be persisted with garbage/NaN coordinates with no test failing.

samples.summary: The missing-rotation test for `resizeFrameToSize` never asserts the normalized `rotation`, so the new `?? 0` normalization output is only half-covered
samples.evidence: The new test at resize.test.ts:153-163 asserts x/y/w/h only. `resizeFrameToSize` spreads `start` (resize.ts:130), so whether the returned frame carries `rotation: 0` or `undefined` depends entirely on `frameAtAnchor` returning the normalized `rotation` (resize.ts:176) — the exact line this delta added. If that were reverted to `start.rotation`, this test would still pass and a frame with `rotation: undefined` would be written back to the store. The sibling `resizeFrameWorld` test (line 170) does assert `rotation: 0` via `toEqual`; this one should too.

samples.summary: `resizeMultiFrames` still propagates `snap.worldFrame.rotation` unnormalized and no test covers a snapshot with no stored rotation
samples.evidence: This delta hardened `resizeFrame`, `resizeFrameWorld` and `frameAtAnchor` against a missing `rotation` and added tests for the latter two, but `resizeMultiFrames` copies `rotation: snap.worldFrame.rotation` verbatim (resize.ts:273). Every `resizeMultiFrames` test in resize.test.ts:191-322 builds snapshots via `frameSnap(..., rotation = 0)` or an explicit rotation, so no test exercises the legacy/imported frame shape the rest of the delta is defending against. A multi-select resize of an imported frame would therefore persist `rotation: undefined` (and poison downstream trigonometry) with a green suite.
searchedFor: read all resizeMultiFrames tests in resize.test.ts

samples.summary: The autofit-commit test never covers the `ancestorHasTransform` skip branch that the new code's correctness argument rests on
samples.evidence: The new editor.ts comment justifies using `localFrame` as the basis by asserting `ancestorHasTransform` restricts the path to translate-only ancestors. rotated-autofit-commit.test.ts only sets up a top-level text element (setup() at line 74 calls `store.addElement(sid, ...)` with no group), so both cases hit the ungrouped path. No case has a rotated/scaled group ancestor (expected: no frame write at all) nor a translating group ancestor (expected: local-space anchored x/y). If that gate regressed, a grouped rotated text box's stored frame would be corrupted on commit with the suite still green.

The frontend already has a natural home for it (`packages/frontend/tests/app/slides/format-panel/{units,pick-sections}.test.ts`) and a running vitest lane, so the gap is not for lack of infra. verdict.reason: A test for anchoredFramePatch exists, just not under the name or glob the reviewer searched: packages/frontend/tests/app/slides/format-panel/rotated-resize.test.tsx. It renders the real FormatPanel over a real MemSlidesStore (the logic under test is not mocked; only the thin SlidesEditor selection surface is stubbed) and commits W/H through the Size & Position inputs, which routes through commitFrame (index.tsx:128) and, with aspect lock on, lockedResize (index.tsx:237) - both of which call anchoredFramePatch. The assertions are behavioral, not vacuous: an independent localToWorld helper checks the unrotated top-left corner stays fixed in world space at rotation pi/4, pi/3, and pi/6 with aspect lock, plus expect(next.x).not.toBeCloseTo(start.x, 3) to prove the compensation actually fired rather than the patch passing through unchanged, and an exact toEqual pinning the unrotated identity case. That directly covers claim (b), the user-visible #1039 panel bug, and the pass-through/identity contract. The file runs in the frontend vitest lane: vite.config.ts:375-380 includes tests/**/*.test.tsx. Only the narrow !Number.isFinite defensive branch (frame-patch.ts:33) is unexercised, which does not sustain the finding's "no test anywhere" major under this lens.
